faq.q: What is the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)?
faq.a: The LRS is an RBI scheme allowing resident Indians to remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year for permissible current or capital account transactions, including investing in foreign stocks and mutual funds.

faq.q: How are capital gains from US stocks taxed in India?
faq.a: For direct investments, gains on stocks held for over 24 months are taxed as LTCG at 12.5%. Gains on stocks held for up to 24 months are STCG, taxed at your income tax slab rate.

faq.q: Are dividends from US stocks taxed in India?
faq.a: Yes, dividends are taxable in India at your applicable income tax slab rate. A 25% withholding tax is levied in the US, which can be claimed as a foreign tax credit under the India-US DTAA.

faq.q: Can NRIs invest in US stocks through LRS?
faq.a: No, the LRS is exclusively for resident individuals. NRIs have different regulations for investing in foreign markets.

faq.q: What is TCS on LRS remittances?
faq.a: As of April 1, 2026, a 20% Tax Collected at Source (TCS) is applicable on LRS remittances exceeding ₹10 lakhs in a financial year for purposes other than education and medical treatment. This TCS can be adjusted against your income tax liability.

faq.q: What documents are needed to invest in US stocks from India?
faq.a: Typically, you will need a valid PAN card, Aadhaar card, and proof of address for KYC verification with your chosen brokerage platform.

faq.q: Are there any limits on the number of remittances under LRS?
faq.a: There is no restriction on the frequency or number of transactions, but the total amount remitted in a financial year must not exceed the USD 250,000 LRS limit.
